current.text: Brooklyn got him from the Celtics in a trade at last season's deadline and recently gave him a contract extension.
He played very well after the trade. In his last nine games he played 23 minutes and averaged 14 points, 3 rebounds, 1.4 steals and 1 block. He finished 265th in category leagues last season.

Brooklyn's projected starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe. The projected bench is Keon Ellis, Noah Clowney, Mo Wagner, Danny Wolf and Nolan Traore.
He is left out of the projected 10-man rotation. The crowded Brooklyn frontcourt hurts his chances of earning a role.
He is a stash option in case Brooklyn gives its young players minutes late in the season. The second half is open: the Nets could hand minutes to Minott, and Porter could be traded.
Houston controls Brooklyn's draft pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins. With nothing to play for, its March minutes are uncertain.
Brooklyn plays 3-4-3 games in our playoff weeks, 10 in total, with one back-to-back. The Nets have 16 back-to-backs this season, tied with Boston for the most in the league.
His projections assume a small role. That puts his points and steals far below the top 250 pool.

durable.text: He is in the 91st percentile in DARKO and has always made an impact on the court. He needs real minutes to matter in fantasy.
